initial_answer: The project provides an MIT-licensed open standard and a cloneable local workspace for organizing project knowledge for AI agents. I can clone it, start Claude Code, and use three Markdown-based folders (what, how, who), with CLAUDE.md for instructions and STATE.md for work in progress. The structure and instructions are inspectable; they do not themselves enforce agent behavior.

prerequisites: Claude Code installed, on PATH, and authenticated with a supported account or API access
A POSIX terminal shell on macOS, Linux, or WSL
An available destination directory; if ~/aDNA already exists, use the existing workspace or clone somewhere else
task_answer.optional_tools: Obsidian is optional; plain Markdown can be read with any editor.
local_file_examples: ~/aDNA/CLAUDE.md — workspace router supplied by the clone
~/aDNA/.adna/how/skills/skill_project_fork.md — instructions for scaffolding the first project
task_answer.where_context_and_governance_live: The workspace router is CLAUDE.md at the clone root; the embedded standard is in .adna/. Each project has its own CLAUDE.md entry point for purpose and rules, STATE.md for live priorities and blockers, MANIFEST.md for overview, and AGENTS.md for routing. Curated knowledge lives in what/context/, policies and roles in who/governance/, and objectives/session handoffs in how/missions/ and how/sessions/. The text names README.md among five governance files. These are instructions an agent must read, not enforcement machinery.
task_answer.expected_result_and_verification: The instructions say the fresh-workspace router sends Claude Code to the project-fork skill, which creates <name>.aDNA/ with what/, how/, who/ and independent Git history. The setup page gives test/ls/git commands to verify files and history, then asks for a fresh agent session inside the project. I found this path in the supplied pages but did not run it.
task_answer.data_handling: The workspace itself is Markdown and makes no network calls after cloning. The command launches Claude Code, whose separate behavior includes sending files it reads to Anthropic according to the setup page.
